correctness.rationale: PASS: The restricted worth v(T)=Σ_{j∈T}[Σ_{i∈T}a_ij+F(B_j(N\T))] is carefully distinguished from recomputation of an induced graph. Assume the insertion-budget inequality F(U⊎{b})≤F(U)+b. For S⊆N define x_j^S=Σ_{i∈S}a_ij+F(B_j(N\S)), giving exact efficiency Σx^S=v(S). For every T⊆S, split external incoming multiset B_j(N\T)=B_j(N\S)⊎B_j(S\T); iterating the budget controls every coalition constraint termwise. Conversely any violating U,b builds an in-star target j with distinguished p and outside sources whose restriction to {p,j} has v({j})>v({p,j})-v({p}) and empty core. Singleton normalization F({b})=b implies v(N\{j})=v(N)-Σ_i a_ij, and every core coordinate ≤ incoming sum, hence uniqueness by efficiency. For min, max, mean and rank statistics the budget follows from order-statistic coordinate Lipschitz bound; the ranks k(m+1)≤k(m)+1 cover medians and quantiles. Independently checked exact rational core inequalities in three-node graphs and four aggregators (C5_OK), not a substitute for universal symbolic proof.

originality.rationale: PASS, qualified: Ryzák–Kroupa arXiv:2605.18157v1 proves total balancedness and core uniqueness for minimum aggregation, and explicitly calls alternative external aggregation stability an open research direction in Section 6. Bandhana–Kroupa–García 2024 introduced the minimum model and incoming-weight core. The new universal iff insertion criterion includes necessity via a strict two-player obstruction and nonminimum stable classes; neither inspected primary result states this. A generic cooperative-game marginal-subadditivity theorem could imply the characterization at a higher level, which remains a priority risk.
residual_risks: An earlier generic balanced-game theorem could subsume the multiset insertion criterion without referring to trust.
Core restriction here retains external exposure to ambient nonmember vertices, not induced-game recomputation.
No Shapley tractability, superadditivity, strategyproofness or signed-weight extension is established.
